title: Hardware-accelerated token hashing fastlane for prompt ingest
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Prefill-side overhead for prompt ingest dominates latency and CPU on high-throughput workloads (multi-tenant hosted API + Dedicated burst). Current UTF-8 normalization + token hashing + packer pipeline runs on the main worker thread and causes tail latency spikes when many short requests arrive in bursts.

Goal: Ship a lightweight, hardware-friendly token-hash "fastlane" that offloads the common-case prompt preprocessing (ASCII/UTF-8 short prefixes, whitespace-only normalization, frequent token prefixes) to a jit-friendly code path that: 1) reduces per-request CPU cost by ~3-5x for small prompts, 2) enables cooperative batching before model prefill, and 3) integrates with kernel-selection hints so serving runtime can prefer low-latency kernels when prefill queue is short.

Scope: Design and implement a non-breaky fastlane that sits before the general tokenizer: a) a fast ASCII scanner + vectorized whitespace normalizer, b) a hardware-accelerated token hash (xxHash64-based, SIMD-friendly) to produce stable cache keys, c) a compact canonicalizer for small prefix-only requests, d) a path that emits a compact prefill token hint for the runtime (estimated token count + first-k token hashes).

Out of scope: Full tokenization correctness for arbitrary Unicode edge cases (falls back to baseline tokenizer), language model token mapping changes, or altering client-visible token ids.

Design decisions: 
- Fastlane triggers: request length < 2KB AND no special control tokens AND UTF-8 valid prefix. This minimizes false positives.
- Hash algorithm: xxHash64 with a small salt per-process to avoid cross-tenant collisions; chosen for speed and good distribution on short strings.
- Cache semantics: LRU local per-worker keyed by (model_variant, token_hash_prefix, normalized_length_bucket). Entries hold prefill token counts and KV cache warm keys. TTL 5m.
- Integration with runtime: expose prefill-hint metadata (est_tokens, hotkey) that kernel-selection can use to prefer low-latency kernel and enable speculative KV cache warm.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Microbench: small prompt median CPU cycles/request reduced by >=3x and p95 latency reduced by >=30% on x86_64 c6i-like instances.
- End-to-end: 5-10% reduction in token cost for multi-tenant hosted workloads under bursty traffic in our synthetic bench.
- No increase in tokenization correctness regressions (existing tokenizer test-suite must pass).
- Feature gated and rolloutable by runtime config with telemetry flags.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged gated rollout → Canary (5% of internal traffic) → Customer beta (selected tenants) → 100% rollout for hosted. Dedicated: opt-in via runtime config in runtime-1.20.
comments: 2026-03-08 - Ava Martinez: Initial RFC posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/fastlane-token-hash. Requesting early perf microbench numbers and review from LangInfra.

2026-03-09 - Liam Chen: Spike prototype implemented (hw_hash_fastlane branch). Microbench sketch: small ascii-only prompts see ~3.6x CPU reduction; added unit tests for ascii fast path and fallback path.
2026-03-10 - Priya Rao (Review): Concern about cross-tenant hash collisions and cache poisoning. Recommend per-worker salt and strict tenant scoping of LRU entries. Added to design notes.

2026-03-11 - Security (Jonas Muller): Confirmed per-worker salt + tenant-scoped cache avoids cross-tenant inference leakage; security_review_required flagged but review completed. See security ticket: https://security.redwood.ai/t/SR-2983
2026-03-12 - Liam Chen: Bench results on c6i: median prefill CPU cycles fell from 58k -> 15k for 128B prompts; p95 latency dropped 34%. Integration hook for kernel hints implemented (PR #3421).
2026-03-12 - QA (Nora Patel): Ran tokenizer regression suite; no failures in baseline + fastlane enabled. Added jitter test for malformed UTF-8 to ensure fallback triggers.

2026-03-13 - Ops (Diego Alvarez): Dependence on warm-KV gating noted; recommend delaying speculative KV warm for high-cost models to avoid wasted GPU cycles. Added rollout gating flag enable_speculative_kv.

2026-03-13 - Liam Chen: Open PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421 (fastlane core), https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/198 (microbench harness). Code review in progress.

2026-03-13 - PM (Sara Li): Marking customer_impact medium. This helps latency-sensitive chat customers but requires monitoring. Added metric dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ingest/fastlane-overview
